newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Bank consolidations continue in Sweden.
newsitem.headline: Bank consolidations continue in Sweden.

text.p: The rapid consolidation of the banking industry in Sweden continued Tuesday when Sparbanken Sverige AB and Foreningsbanken AB said they were combining to become the country's second-largest bank.

The deal, announced just a day after the two banks said they were in merger talks, followed Monday's announcement of the merger of Handelsbanken and Stadshypotek AB, which created the largest bank in Sweden.
Analysts expected the two amalgamations to drive two other banks, S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, back into negotiations that collapsed two weeks ago.
Swedish banks have been consolidating rapidly to compete with their larger European rivals and protect themselves from possible takeovers.
"The boards of Foreningsbanken and Sparbanken have decided to propose a merger and form ForeningsSparbanken," they said in a statement.
The two banks also posted their 1996 results Tuesday, with Sparbanken's better than expected and Foreningsbanken's in line with expectations.

Officials of the two banks told a press conference that merger costs would be 2 billion crowns ($268.2 million) at the most and savings of 1.5 billion crowns ($201.2 million) a year would be realised by the year 2000.
The savings would be achieved at least partly by axing about 2,000 jobs from the combined work force of around 14,000, the companies said.
The merger came as no surprise.

Analysts said that Sparbanken Sverige, known as Swedbank in Sweden, had been interested in Foreningsbanken since 1994 and its interest became more intense in the midst of the current restructuring of the sector.
"So the merger has not come as any real surprise," said one London-based banking analyst.
The merged bank will be the second-largest in Sweden with combined assets of 657 billion crowns ($88 billion), compared with Handelsbanken/Stadhypoteks assets of 870 billion crowns ($116.7 billion).
Swedbank reported a 20 percent rise in operating profit to 5.30 billion crowns ($710.8 million).
Foreningsbanken reported a 14 percent increase in operating profit to 1.16 billion crowns ($155.6 million).
Handelsbanken also posted 1996 results, announcing a 33 percent jump in operating profit to 6.72 billion crowns ($901.3 million), which was above market expectations.
"Swedish banks are definitely back on recovery," Thorn said. "The question now is how they can continue to maintain the momentum."
